meta.notes: Contradiction searches: blank-field rejection policy status, Docketwise positive reviews, incumbent feature pages (N/A autofill, reverse autofill, two-way sync, multilingual intake, AI document capture). Capterra, G2, Software Advice, TrustRadius, Reddit, LollyLaw.com and Mitratech pages were unfetchable (robots/403), so review evidence relies on Software Finder and SourceForge; Reddit voice comes from one mirrored post. Founder claims not found in public sources: LollyLaw week-long outage, INSZoom/Tracker support decline, broken Clio/MyCase accounting sync. Docketwise is owned by 8am (MyCase/AffiniPay), not Clio. No source quantified paralegal hours per case. Prospects: 21 US immigration firms from their own sites; size is stated for only 5; no technology stack evidence for any; ICP ids were not provided by context so icp_id is null. Locke Immigration's cited page gives no location (geography left null).

evidence.title: USCIS rejects certain application forms for incompleteness if any fields are left blank (Immigration Policy Tracking Project)
evidence.quote: Under the policy, USCIS rejected applications that left any question in the application unanswered, even where the question was not applicable—for example where the applicant failed to include a response for middle name because they have no middle name. Additionally, USCIS rejected applications where the applicant wrote “none” or “not applicable” instead of “N/A.”
evidence.statement: Under the 2019-2020 'no blank space' policy USCIS rejected forms for unanswered not-applicable fields and for writing 'none' instead of 'N/A'.

evidence.title: USCIS rejects certain application forms for incompleteness if any fields are left blank (Immigration Policy Tracking Project)
evidence.quote: the settlement agreement prevents the agency from adopting a similar rejection policy with respect to other immigration forms unless authorized by statute or lawfully implemented through regulations. … On April 1, 2021, USCIS confirmed that for all forms it has reverted to the form rejection criteria it applied before October 2019 regarding blank responses.
evidence.statement: The blank-field rejection policy was rescinded in 2021 and a settlement limits its return, weakening the urgency of automatic N/A/None filling.

evidence.title: USCIS Increases Rejections for Incomplete Immigration Forms (Minsky McCormick & Hallagan)
evidence.quote: If USCIS rejects a petition due to a trivial omission, like writing “none” rather than “N/A” into the field for middle name — even when an applicant does not have a middle name — the certification may expire and the applicant may not have enough time obtain a new one.
evidence.statement: An immigration firm describes how a trivial form omission can cause a rejection that makes time-limited evidence expire.

evidence.title: USCIS Rejected My Application? 7 Mistakes That Cause It (CitizenPath)
evidence.quote: USCIS lockbox facilities processed more than 10 million applications in fiscal year 2025 and rejected 11% of them. That works out to roughly 1.1 million packages returned in a single year.
evidence.statement: About 11% of lockbox filings (~1.1M packages) were rejected in FY2025 (all filers, not only law firms).

evidence.title: USCIS Rejected My Application? 7 Mistakes That Cause It (CitizenPath)
evidence.quote: USCIS reports that the single most common reason is an incorrect fee amount. Payment problems, signature problems, and outdated forms account for a large share of the rest.
evidence.statement: The most common rejection reason is the wrong fee, not mis-filled form fields; payment, signature and outdated editions follow.

evidence.title: USCIS Rejected My Application? 7 Mistakes That Cause It (CitizenPath)
evidence.quote: USCIS does not assign a receipt date to a rejected application. In the agency's terms, the filing never happened. … A rejection in those situations can cost you a place in line.
evidence.statement: A rejected filing gets no receipt date, which can cost priority/deadline position.

evidence.title: New Form I-485 Edition Required September 18, 2026 (Ahluwalia Law Offices)
evidence.quote: USCIS has stated that there is no grace period for the revised edition, which is why the agency released a preview version of the form and its instructions in advance. … Both directions carry consequences. Filing the new edition early results in rejection, and filing the old edition late results in rejection.
evidence.statement: The 09/18/26 I-485 edition had no grace period; wrong edition either way means rejection, so form templates must switch on an exact date.

evidence.title: USCIS announces new form edition for several forms with no grace period (Immigration Policy Tracking Project)
evidence.quote: USCIS announced a new form edition, dated 01/20/2025, for 7 forms: … The new form edition takes effect immediately, with no grace period for prior editions.
evidence.statement: In early 2025 USCIS issued new editions of a dozen forms at once, initially with no grace period (later relaxed after an AILA lawsuit).

summary.statement: Paralegals and legal assistants gather client information and documents, then prepare USCIS forms from it under attorney review.
Most firms use dedicated immigration software (INSZoom, Cerenade, LawLogix, Tracker, Docketwise, Clio); a minority fill USCIS PDFs in Adobe Acrobat or use Google Drive.
Some firms run a forms tool alongside a general practice-management tool such as Clio, which is the multi-tool setup the idea describes.
Without form software, the same client data is retyped across several forms.

Complaints exist: technical issues with forms are a recurring Docketwise complaint, one small-firm reviewer calls it a glorified PDF filler that does not integrate with Clio as advertised, and a paralegal reports errors when saving forms in a legacy tool.
Forms-to-Clio integrations are described as one-way, which creates double entry.
Many small-firm reviewers rate Docketwise forms as accurate and frequently updated, so the dissatisfaction is not universal.
The specific complaint that edits on the PDF never reach the client record is contradicted by incumbents: LollyLaw advertises two-way form-to-record sync and Docketwise lists Reverse Autofill.
No public evidence was found of the LollyLaw week-long outage or of INSZoom/Tracker support worsening after acquisition.
Rejections are common and costly: about 11% of lockbox filings were rejected in FY2025, and a rejected filing gets no receipt date, which can cost priority or deadline position.
Trivial field errors ('none' instead of 'N/A', blank middle name) caused rejections under the 2019-2020 policy.
That blank-field policy was rescinded in 2021, and the most common rejection reason now is the wrong fee rather than mis-filled fields.
Using the wrong form edition is an active rejection risk (e.g. the I-485 09/18/26 edition had no grace period).
No firm-level data was found on how many hours or how much money a rejection costs a law firm.
No verifiable source quantified paralegal hours per case for data entry or corrections; vendor figures found in search could not be fetched or cited.
Most immigration lawyers work in very small firms (about 76% of AILA members in firms with three or fewer lawyers), so the owner-attorney is likely the buyer.
Paralegals can run the evaluation: one paralegal was tasked with researching and demoing replacement software.
Case-management software is described as one of the most expensive items in an immigration firm's budget.
Creating government forms and saving client information in them was the top-rated feature (4.54/5) in a 2019 survey of immigration lawyers; a client intake portal scored 3.90.
Keeping form editions current is critical because USCIS releases editions with little or no grace period.

Several proposed wedge features already exist in incumbents: N/A autofill (Docketwise), reverse autofill/two-way sync (Docketwise, LollyLaw), document data capture (Docketwise IQ), and edition-change handling within days.
Incumbent pricing is $80-$140 per user per month, consistent with the $119 solo price hypothesis.
Incumbents already offer multilingual, mobile-friendly client questionnaires: Docketwise (auto-translated, smartphones) and MyCase (12 languages).
Docketwise's AI data capture already reads immigration documents into forms, overlapping the photo-check idea.
No public evidence was found on how firms handle clients with limited technology access, or on whether automatic name/date cross-checks of document photos are wanted.

new_unknowns.question: Given that Docketwise and LollyLaw already offer reverse autofill/two-way sync and N/A autofill, what concrete failure do paralegals still hit when correcting forms?
Would firms run a second forms tool alongside their existing case-management system for new cases only, or does the tool need billing/CRM to replace incumbents?

competitors.name: 8am DocketWise
competitors.description: Immigration case management with Smart Forms filled from one multilingual intake questionnaire, N/A autofill, reverse autofill, AI document data capture, e-filing; owned by 8am (MyCase/AffiniPay), not Clio.
competitors.pricing_note: Basic $80/user/month on docketwise.com; Software Finder lists $90 / $120 / $140 per user per month (Sep 2026).

sentiment.statement: Reviewers praise ease of use and accurate, frequently updated forms.
Technical issues with forms are a frequent complaint; one reviewer calls it overpriced and poorly integrated with Clio.

competitors.name: LollyLaw
competitors.description: All-in-one immigration practice management (intake, LollyForms, billing) owned by Paradigm; advertises two-way form/record sync and form-edition notifications.

sentiment.statement: A reviewer says customer service is hit or miss; other reviewers praise support.

competitors.name: eimmigration by Cerenade
competitors.description: Immigration case management and forms; claims 17,000+ users and was the second most used product in the 2019 survey.

sentiment.statement: One reviewer dislikes that only one user can access an account at a time.

competitors.name: Mitratech INSZoom
competitors.description: Immigration case management aimed at law firms, corporate HR, universities and large nonprofits; most used system in the 2019 survey.

competitors.name: Tracker (ImmigrationTracker, Mitratech)
competitors.description: Immigration case management product used by larger firms (7% of 2019 survey respondents).

competitors.name: 8am MyCase (immigration)
competitors.description: General practice management with immigration form-filling in 12 client languages and form data linked to case files.

competitors.name: Clio
competitors.description: General practice management used for client management and billing alongside a separate forms tool; 6% of 2019 survey respondents used it for immigration.

competitors.name: Adobe Acrobat + USCIS fillable PDFs
competitors.description: Filling official USCIS PDFs by hand, sometimes with Google Drive for files.

competitors.name: CitizenPath
competitors.description: DIY filing service for self-filers that checks answers, handles not-applicable fields, edition and fee checks; an alternative to hiring a firm for simple cases.

current_solutions.statement: Most immigration firms prepare forms in dedicated case-management software (INSZoom, Cerenade, LawLogix, Tracker, Docketwise, LollyLaw), often alongside Clio or MyCase for billing.
Paralegals gather client data and documents and prepare forms, with attorney review.
A minority fill USCIS PDFs manually in Adobe Acrobat.
Leading tools already include multilingual mobile intake, N/A autofill, two-way sync and AI document capture.
